extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals, corporate communications teams, crisis communicators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for corporate crisis communications response after a hazardous incident, focusing on timeliness, tone, leadership visibility, media strategy, and remediation documentation. Aimed at shaping public narrative and rebuilding trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of initial response
rubrics_metrics.description: The consensus among PR experts is that Norfolk Southern’s initial response to the Feb. 3 incident was slow-footed, tentative and, overall, wholly inadequate to the magnitude of the situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond promptly and decisively; avoid slow, tentative, procedural messaging at the outset of a major incident. Early inaction or delay allows other actors and narratives to frame the story and exacerbates local alarm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone: avoid impersonal, defensive or tone-deaf messaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Early communications consisted mainly of long-winded and impersonal written statements... many of the company’s media statements have been unnecessarily defensive and tone deaf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use empathetic, human, and plain-language messaging rather than long, impersonal statements. Avoid taking a defensive posture (e.g., publicly chastising critics or claiming 'misinformation')—that alienates affected communities and fuels negative coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence at stakeholder events and engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: At a time when the EPA and Ohio Governor DeWine fielded questions from residents at an open town hall, Norfolk Southern cancelled its appearance, citing safety concerns. By the time CEO Alan Shaw was on the scene, the damage had been done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be present where stakeholders gather (town halls, community meetings). Canceling or failing to appear surrenders the forum to others and undermines trust. Prioritize face-to-face (or live) engagement when safety allows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership authenticity and performance on camera
rubrics_metrics.description: CEO Shaw has taken center stage but his performance has been rehearsed and wooden... During a CNN-staged 'town hall' Shaw was mute while a life-long resident... pleaded for Shaw’s help and declared 'your company stinks.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaders should demonstrate authenticity, empathy, and readiness to engage; canned or overly rehearsed appearances come off as insincere. Prepare leaders to acknowledge concerns, show compassion, and convey concrete next steps rather than platitudes like 'we're going to make this right' without specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual storytelling: create compelling visuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Apparently, Shaw and his PR team haven’t learned the first lesson of TV journalism: The story is visual. Pictures drive coverage... If Norfolk Southern wants to control and eventually end the crisis, they need to create their own visuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactively generate positive, newsworthy visuals (e.g., crews delivering fresh soil, employees planting community green space, leaders working on-site). Visuals should document remediation and humanize the response to influence TV and social coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document tangible remediation and community assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: The company pledged to donate $300,000 to the East Palestine School District... donate $850,000 to the local fire department and a $220,000 reimbursement to fund new equipment for first responders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Announce and visibly execute concrete remediation steps and assistance (financial pledges, equipment, cleanup work). But accompany such steps with visible action and documentation so they are perceived as more than PR gestures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be available to cameras while doing real work
rubrics_metrics.description: Shaw doesn’t need to comment on the record or answer hostile questions, as long as he’s available for cameras, ideally while working at a desk in Norfolk Southern’s new East Palestine-based 'Office of the Cleanup.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make leadership accessible to media in non-adversarial, action-oriented settings—e.g., working on-site—so cameras capture tangible engagement. Availability can be off-the-record but visible; optics matter even when legal/technical answers are deferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control and reset the narrative through ongoing documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Ultimately, Norfolk Southern will never fully repair its tattered reputation until it can take control of the narrative. The company’s PR needs to re-set the story and document the restoration of East Palestine from the ground up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop a proactive narrative arc focused on remediation and recovery; continuously document progress (photos, videos, timelines, updates) to replace initial damaging imagery with restorative images and stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor media strategy to medium (especially television)
rubrics_metrics.description: These are steps in the right direction. But more could be done, especially for television... Pictures drive coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the different demands of TV vs. print/digital. For TV, prioritize visuals, on-camera availability, and staged remediation activities. Avoid strategies that look good in press releases but have poor TV imagery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clear information on liability, compensation, and next steps
rubrics_metrics.description: In an extended interview with CNBC, he was unable to address questions of legal liability and financial compensation. That’s understandable, but lines like 'we’re going to make this right,' just beg more questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While legal constraints may limit specifics early on, offer clear guidance about how affected people will be supported, how claims/compensation will be handled, and timelines for next steps. Vague reassurance without process or pathways to redress breeds distrust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain frequent, transparent updates (e.g., dedicated website)
rubrics_metrics.description: The company has dedicated part of its website to daily updates and information for affected residents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide regular, easily accessible updates (daily if necessary) via a central information hub. Transparency about monitoring, testing, and remediation progress helps counter rumors and reduce anxiety.
